segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, so for the calibration tracking rollout, I have you at 50 named users, right? Thirty-eight techs, eight supervisors, and four quality admins.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That's right. We may add two more techs in August, but for the initial PO, 50 is clean.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Okay. The pricing sheet has 50 seats at $42,000 annually, plus a one-time implementation fee of $6,800. That includes the instrument import, two admin trainings, and the first workflow setup.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Works for budget. On invoicing, can you split the implementation fee onto the first invoice and keep the subscription annual, net 30?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, that's standard. First invoice would show $48,800 total, net 30, and then the renewal invoice next year would just be the subscription unless you add services.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. We need go-live by July 15 because our audit starts August 6. Is that realistic if we sign by June 14?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes. If signature and PO are in by June 14, kickoff the week of June 17, data import by June 28, user acceptance the week of July 8, and go-live July 15 is comfortable.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. Contract term, just twelve months? Our finance team doesn't want a three-year commitment yet.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Twelve months is fine. The order form will show a July 15 start date and a July 14 end date next year. No multi-year language.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Send the order form to me and copy Dana in procurement. If it matches what we discussed, I'll route the PO tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Will do. I'll send it this afternoon with the seat count, pricing, net 30 terms, and the July 15 implementation schedule called out.
